ov: Long-nosed members of the raccoon family from the Americas. They are active by day: females and young travel in noisy bands, rooting for invertebrates with their flexible, upturned snouts, while adult males live alone.
len: 33–69 cm, plus a tail that can be as long again
rg: South America, Central America, Mexico and the southwestern United States.
df: Omnivores that mainly eat ground litter and invertebrates such as tarantulas.
fx: Bands usually number 4 to 25, and adult males join them only in the short mating season.
Coatis live up to seven years in the wild and about 14 in captivity.
